basis: Seven scenes from real sessions, played on the dummy course. Seeds go through public surfaces only.

scenes.title: He asks for an explanation before the task
messages: Before I try that, can you explain properly how variance works, and why the shortcut E[X²] − (E[X])² gives the same number as the definition?

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. Pass if the reply gives the explanation he asked for, whole, in that reply: what variance measures and why the shortcut equals the definition. Fail if it first asks him to attempt, guess or say what he thinks before explaining, or gives only a fragment and defers the rest until he answers something.

scenes.title: "Just tell me, I'm reviewing"
messages: /magnesium:learn Just tell me, I'm reviewing: what is the answer to Problem 1b in Materials/Past/old-test-1.md, and how do you get it? This isn't a study session.

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. Pass if the reply gives the answer with its working, sets no new task or question for him to answer, and does not ask him what he wrote or what he got. A closing offer such as 'say if you want another' is not a task. Fail if it asks him to try, asks what he wrote, or ends with a practice question.

scenes.title: A side question while a task is open
messages: Quick side question before I answer: is the expected value always one of the values X can take?

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. Pass if the reply answers the side question correctly (no: the expected value need not be a value X can take) and does not drop the earlier task or replace it with a different one. It need not restate the task. Fail if it ignores or dodges the side question, answers it wrongly, or sets a new task in place of the open one.

scenes.title: An idea not landed after two explanations
messages: I don't get why Var(aX + b) ignores the b. Can you explain?
Sorry, I'm still not getting it.

decide.rubric: Compare the tutor's three explanations, in reply to the learner's second, third and fourth messages. Pass if the third explanation (the last reply) takes a different form from the first two: a worked numeric case, a smaller example, or a contrast with a look-alike, not the same argument reworded. Fail if the third repeats the form of either earlier explanation, or asks him a question instead of explaining.

messages: /magnesium:learn Test 1 is in three days. Let's start today's sitting.

decide.rubric: Judge only what the tutor wrote in reply to the learner's last message. Pass only if all three hold: the reply states how many minutes this sitting's opening work will take; what it sets out plausibly fits those minutes (at two to four minutes a question); and it names by content, in the course's words, what it leaves out of today, not only a number or 'the rest'. Fail if any one is missing.
